outcome: response to treatment (absence of ICH and platelet count >= 50 000/mL at birth)
cohort: The study included 91 pregnant women with 225 pregnancies diagnosed with recurrent fetal and neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia (FNAIT) and managed at a single tertiary referral center between 1992 and 2024.
finding: Among IVIG-treated pregnancies, 82.6% exhibited a good response to treatment, but a good response in one FNAIT-affected pregnancy did not guarantee successful treatment in subsequent pregnancies.
mod_finding: Fetal blood sampling at 37 weeks' gestation determined the mode of delivery, with vaginal delivery allowed when the fetal platelet count was >= 50 000/mL.
